ledger.note: 795: Charlemagne establishes the Spanish March in the eastern Pyrenees. 'It was established in c. 795 by Charlemagne.' It begins with Roussillon (c. 760), Girona (785) and Ribagorza and Pallars (c. 790); Louis the Pious was king of Aquitaine from 781.
798: Urgell and Cerdanya are added to the march. The page gives the year, not the previous holder; the Umayyad lords of the Pyrenees are read as the counterpart.

801: Louis the Pious takes Barcelona. The Frankish army gathered on 20 August 800, the siege began in October 800, Louis arrived in February 801, and the wali Harun surrendered on 4 April 801; Bera, son of William of Gellone, became the first count.

The region is the Aragon valley only (Cliopatria's County of Aragon), not the province of Huesca; the page also says Navarre and Aragon 'formally' were not in the march. Reviewer finding applied.

region.text: the whole march, passed to the hereditary counts

ledger.note: 897: Wilfred the Hairy dies on 11 August and his holdings pass to his sons, ending the Frankish march of appointed counts. He was 'the first to pass his vast holdings as an inheritance to his sons'. Urgell and Cerdanya were his from 870 (June, Charles the Bald), Barcelona, Girona and Besalú from 878 (Louis the Stammerer), Ausona repopulated from 879 (County of Osona page; the Wilfred the Hairy page says 885-886); Miró held Roussillon, passed to Sunyer II in 895. The march is read as ending here; the Barcelona counts became de facto independent only in 985-988.

wars.name: Frankish siege of Barcelona
wars.outcome: Louis the Pious, King of Aquitaine, took Barcelona from the wali Harun, who surrendered on 4 April 801 after a siege begun in October 800; Bera became first count.

wars.name: Frankish attempts on Huesca and Tortosa
wars.outcome: The Carolingians tried to take Tortosa and Huesca (807, 812) 'without success'; the Llobregat valley border was reinforced.

wars.name: Battle of Pancorbo
wars.outcome: The Moors defeated the Carolingians in 816. The page says Pamplona (Iñigo Arista) 'broke away from the Spanish March' and the County of Aragon 'shortly thereafter in 820', but also that Navarre and Aragon 'formally' were not in the march (Duchy of Vasconia); only Aragon's 820 loss is booked here.
wars.note: The page gives the battle in one line and no consequence for the march's border.

notes: Written for eu-07-x from four pages (Spanish March, County of Barcelona, Siege of Barcelona (801), Wilfred the Hairy). The Spanish March page has no infobox, no area and no end date; 897 (Wilfred the Hairy's death and the first inherited holdings) is chosen as the end because Cliopatria's Barcelona, Besalú, Berga and Roussillon rows begin in 896-898; the Barcelona page's 985-988 independence is the later end some would choose. Overlaps: Cliopatria draws Ribagorza (866), Urgell (870) and Pallars (875) as separate rows before 897 and the west-franks dossier books those cells as 870/872/878 losses to those rows; the March's cells there duplicate them and the compile should prefer the county rows. Kingdom-of-the-franks books only Barcelona's 801 gain (from emirate-of-cordoba) and must subtract this dossier's land (and the March is inside Cliopatria's Frankish shapes of 801-843 or not, which the Franks' owner must check). Septimania (Narbonne, Carcassonne), the 'Gothic March', Conflent and Vallespir beyond Roussillon, and Empúries are not separately dated by the pages and are not drawn except Roussillon (c. 760) and the Gerona province. 844 (Sunifred I count of Barcelona) and Bernard of Septimania are not on the pages as territorial events. 870 (June) and 878 (Barcelona, Girona, Besalú to Wilfred) are appointments within the march and are not ledger events. Gazetteer names needed (drawn as lon/lat circles): Pallars, Ribagorza, Urgell, Cerdanya, Osona/Ausona, Empúries (regions); Vic, La Seu d'Urgell, Puigcerdà (places). Wikidata id left null (page not mapped). REPAIR 2026-10-25 (reviewer fail): (1) Aragon is now the Aragon valley only (Cliopatria's County of Aragon 830 shape, 15 cells) instead of the province of Huesca (67 cells); the Spanish March page says Navarre and Aragon 'formally' were not in the march, so this is a confidence-2 reading of the 798-802 castles and the 820 breakaway; the alternative is to drop Aragon and the 802/820 events. (2) The 798-816 Pamplona vassal pair is dropped: the page puts Navarre/Pamplona under the Duchy of Vasconia, and kingdom-of-the-franks books Pamplona's loss in 825, so kingdom-of-pamplona is not needed here; the page does say (Pancorbo sentence) that Pamplona 'broke away from the Spanish March' in 816, a contradiction left in the war outcome. (3) Ausona (Osona around Vic) leaves the march in 826 (rebellion of Aissó and Guillemó, with Córdoba's help) and returns in 879 (Wilfred's repopulation): from the County of Osona page, because the 'Aizo' URL is a song and 'Aizo of Ausona' and 'Aissó' do not exist; the Wilfred the Hairy page has 885-886 for the county's re-creation (the earlier 879 is used). The gazetteer has no Osona, Ausona or Vic: a 25 km circle at lon 2.25, lat 41.93 is used, intersected with Barcelona province. County of Osona also says Osona was 'considered to be part of the County of Barcelona throughout' 826-879 (a title). Empúries 'first records ... from 812' (Spanish March page) is still not drawn.
